input: 금요일 미용실 넣고 토요일 AWS 2시간, 일요일 운동 넣어줘
notes: A3-5's canonical example, straight from the epic text -- 3 new items in one message. `expected` is deliberately empty: item count/contents live inside `items`, an array of per-item objects, which grade.ts's argsMismatches only checks at the top level of `expected` -- not worth extending the grader for one fixture's benefit (same reasoning schedule-parity.jsonl/schedule-edit.jsonl already applied to model-phrasing-dependent fields). Checked via manual review: exactly 3 items, dates resolving to Fri/Sat/Sun, the AWS item carrying estimatedMinutes 120.

input: 내일 점심 약속이랑 저녁에 헬스장 일정 추가해줘
notes: 2 new items, same day -- tests the model reaches for the batch tool even when both items share a date (not just a multi-day request like batch-001).

Negative case for A3-5 -- a genuinely single-item create must still use propose_schedule, not propose_schedule_batch, even though both tools are available. Guards against the model over-applying the new batch tool to every create request.

input: 다음 주에 할 일 다섯 개 정리해서 넣어줘: 세탁소 가기, 병원 예약, 책 반납, 이발, 자동차 점검
notes: 5-item batch, all tasks (entryKind: task) rather than timed events -- exercises the cap's midpoint, not just batch-001's 3-item example. Manual review: all 5 titles present, no item silently dropped.

input: 이번 주 일정 중에 겹치는 거 있으면 다 완료 처리해줘
notes: Deliberately NOT a propose_schedule_batch case -- this is a bulk UPDATE/completion request (the 2026-09-15 incident that motivated the epic's Goal text), which propose_schedule_batch does not cover (create-only, see A3-1's own scope note on the epic issue). A well-behaved model should ask for clarification (which items, since '겹치는 거' is vague) rather than either inventing a batch-complete action with no tool for it, or silently doing nothing. Characterizes the known batch-update gap this epic didn't close, not a bug in what shipped.
